findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file is missing, unreadable, or not UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))? and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: std::fs is imported and used inside load_shards which fuses file I/O, parsing, domain construction, and console side-effects into one function
findings.failure_mode: pure domain logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation; shell work (I/O, logging) bleeds into the functional core
findings.fix: split into: shell function read_and_parse(path: &str) -> Result<String, LoadError>, and core function parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effect embedded inside the mapping closure that builds domain records
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic is no longer pure or deterministic; logging leaks into the core, breaking referential transparency and making output non-reproducible
findings.fix: move all console output to the shell layer; parse_records must return data with no side effects

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing into a Vec<String> produced by split(',')
findings.failure_mode: a line with zero or one comma panics with IndexOutOfBounds; hostile or truncated input aborts processing
findings.fix: use parts.get(0).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? and parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?, or let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input and on empty string after trim
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV field aborts the entire collection instead of returning a typed parse error

findings.problem: (...) as u16 performs a lossy narrowing cast from u32 to u16; values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently wrap to 0..=2790403
findings.failure_mode: invalid domain values are accepted silently, corrupting data integrity without any error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)? instead of as u16

findings.problem: raw string primitives from CSV splitting cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; caller can construct Record with any name string and any u16 value directly
findings.failure_mode: illegal domain states are representable; no validation occurs at the parse boundary so invalid names and out-of-range values enter the core
findings.fix: create Record::new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Record, ParseError> with validation, or use newtype for name and value; parse with split_once and smart constructor

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> with no Result type; all errors (I/O, parse, bounds, allocation) are silently converted to panics via unwrap()
findings.failure_mode: callers have no way to distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from overflow; error recovery is impossible
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is an enum with Io(ParseError), Invalid, Overflow variants

findings.problem: No cap on the number of records; no try_reserve on the output Vec; unbounded external file can cause arbitrary heap allocation
findings.failure_mode: a sufficiently large input file exhausts available memory, causing OOM kill instead of graceful error
findings.fix: enforce a domain max record count before collecting; call Vec::with_capacity or values.try_reserve(max).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)?

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String with no validation; Record.value is a raw u16 with no range invariant or newtype
findings.failure_mode: illegal states (empty names, names with control characters, values exceeding domain bounds) are representable at the type level
findings.fix: use a Name newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and character constraints; value can stay u16 only if parse-time bounds enforcement is proven

findings.problem: load_shards fuses three responsibilities: (1) filesystem I/O via fs::read_to_string, (2) CSV parsing with split, and (3) domain Record construction — all in one function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test parsing logic without a real file on disk; cannot mock I/O without mocking the entire function
findings.fix: extract shell layer: fn load_shards(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> { let text = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))?; parse_records(&text) } and core fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: line.split(',') produces variable-length slices; no guard against single-field or empty lines before indexing parts[0] and parts[1]
findings.failure_mode: empty lines, trailing newlines, or truncated rows panic at parts[0] or parts[1] access
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on (Some((name, val)), _) to destructurally bind with guaranteed indices

residual_risk: Review found 12 BLOCKER findings including panic surfaces (unwrap on I/O and parse), unchecked indexing into split results, lossy narrowing cast (u32 as u16), hidden I/O and logging in pure parsing logic, unbounded allocation, absence of typed error taxonomy, and raw primitive domain state (String name, u16 value). No commands were run; the code will not compile cleanly under strict clippy gates due to unwraps in non-Result-returning context and indexing_slicing violations. Functional Core / Imperative Shell is entirely violated: I/O, logging, parsing, and domain construction are fused in one function. Typestate, newtypes, and smart constructors are absent.
